page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FXmsv2 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 336.0 GB of RAM, yielding an exceptionally high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. It operates on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2278.0 placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong results at 34.66 GB/sec and 14.28 GB/sec respectively. However, multi-core and multi-threaded operations are relatively weak due to the low core count, as evidenced by a weak stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 4437.25 and a weak bzip3 multi-threaded decompression score. Memory bandwidth for large, uncached blocks is also limited, though small-block cached read bandwidth averages 345.21 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform at average tiers, with Redis handling 6.3 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of this server configuration is its extreme memory capacity paired with a very low compute core count. This makes it highly cost-efficient for workloads that require massive memory footprints but do not demand heavy parallel CPU processing. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, large in-memory databases, caching layers, and specific text-processing tasks, whereas highly parallelized tasks like software compilation or large-scale LLM inference will be constrained by the 4 vCPU limit.
